_comment: VIDEO generation. A MOTION brief, not a face description: the face
comes from the still render, which is why still.json is generated
first. Re-describing the face in text is how identity drifts.
Built from PERSONALITY + GENDER only - NOTHING is derived from the
display name, because names are placeholders. Assistants are NORMAL
PEOPLE, deliberately not classic secretaries: no headset, no blazer,
no reception desk, no name badge (owner, 2026-07-28).
Per supacharge-characters.md 3, Bianca is not a different character -
same role and scripts as Mandy, only a different face and voice - so
these two files differ in the person and in nothing else.

reference_image.source: appearance/still.json -> the approved headshot or studio render
reference_image.why: text alone produces a different person every run; the reference locks the face. Never pull a still out of a clip - video frames are motion-blurred and compressed.

identity_lock: shoulder-length box braids, half-up loose bun
gap between the upper front teeth
small mole high on the right cheek

performance.energy: approachable and unhurried; the person who makes a nervous student feel it is fine to ask
performance.spoken_register: warm, clear, conversational; friendly without being bubbly
performance.body: stands or sits relaxed, shoulders loose, head tilted slightly as if listening; one hand gesturing small and close to the body
performance.expression: warm, attentive, mid-listening rather than mid-presenting - the face of someone who has just been asked a question and is about to answer it kindly

camera.camera: 24-30fps, 50mm equivalent, static or very slow push-in
camera.framing: 9:16 vertical - head and shoulders in the upper two thirds, room for captions below
camera.continuity: same wardrobe, same hair, same jewellery across a session; regenerate from continuity_anchors rather than re-describing from scratch

audio.dialogue: supplied separately from this assistant's own assets (intro/, handover/, signoff/, timekeeping/)
audio.note: lip-sync to supplied audio where the model supports it; never let the model invent speech for a host

shots.prompt: Vertical 9:16 talking-to-camera clip. THE PERSON FROM THE REFERENCE IMAGE - do not restyle the face, hair, clothing or age. Energy: approachable and unhurried; the person who makes a nervous student feel it is fine to ask Delivery: warm, clear, conversational; friendly without being bubbly Plain studio backdrop, softly out of focus. Head and shoulders in the upper two thirds, clear space below for captions. Natural handheld micro-movement, real-photography look, 8 seconds.

negative_prompt: cartoon, illustration, 3d render, cgi, airbrushed skin, waxy skin, plastic sheen, over-saturated colours, HDR halos, extra fingers, malformed hands, distorted ears, text, watermark, logo, subtitles, teeth artefacts, dead eyes, glassy doll eyes, vacant thousand-yard stare, identical catchlights in both eyes, flat matte irises, eyes looking through the camera, call-centre headset, telephone headset, earpiece, corporate receptionist, secretary, reception desk, office cubicle, business suit, severe tight bun, name badge, lanyard, clipboard, stock-photo customer-service pose, hands clasped in front like a hostess, air-hostess styling, generic stock-photo smile, classroom, chalkboard, school desks
_identity_lock_note: COPIED from still.json continuity_anchors - never edited here. The face lives in the reference render; duplicating its description is how the two files drift apart.
_no_face_description: This file must NEVER describe the face, hair, wardrobe or age - that belongs to still.json and the reference render.
